ActiveDirectoryAuthenticationProviderOpt.summary: Property bag used by the constructor.
ActiveDirectoryAuthenticationProviderOpt.remarks:
Prefer this options-bag constructor over the positional-argument overloads in new code. Additional options can be added here in future versions without introducing new constructor overloads.
enables the native authentication broker on Windows, Linux and macOS. Each platform expects a different redirect URI and requires an operating system component that may not be installed.

DeviceCodeFlowCallback.summary: Optional device-code-flow callback invoked for SqlAuthenticationMethod.ActiveDirectoryDeviceCodeFlow. When , the provider's default callback (which writes the device-code instructions to the console) is used.

ApplicationClientId.summary: Optional Entra ID application (client) id. When , the SqlClient first-party application id is used and broker mode is forced on (regardless of ).

UseWamBroker.summary: Controls whether the provider uses the native authentication broker for interactive authentication: the Windows Account Manager (WAM) on Windows, and the msalruntime broker on Linux and macOS. Defaults to when you provide a custom . Otherwise, broker mode is used automatically.
UseWamBroker.remarks:
Broker mode requires the Entra ID app registration for to list a redirect URI under "Mobile and desktop applications". Each broker uses a different one:
Windows: ms-appx-web://microsoft.aad.brokerplugin/{clientId}.
Linux: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/nativeclient. This URI must be explicitly enabled on the app registration.
macOS, bundled application: msauth.{bundleIdentifier}://auth, where bundleIdentifier is the host application's CFBundleIdentifier.
macOS, executable or script that is not a bundled application: msauth.com.msauth.unsignedapp://auth.
The broker also requires an operating system component: the Windows Account Manager on Windows 10 or later, the microsoft-identity-broker package on Linux, or the Microsoft Company Portal on macOS.
On Linux the broker is only used on x64 glibc runtimes where the native msalruntime library can be loaded. That library is not published for other Linux runtime identifiers, and it links against libwebkit2gtk, libsecret and libx11, which are absent from most server and container images. Linux hosts that cannot load it use the system browser instead.
On macOS, a bundled application cannot use the built-in SqlClient application id, because its redirect URI is derived from the application's own bundle identifier. Set to an Entra ID application you control and register msauth.{bundleIdentifier}://auth on it. Connecting with the built-in application id from a bundled application throws, except for SqlAuthenticationMethod.ActiveDirectoryDeviceCodeFlow, which does not use the broker.
On macOS, MSAL requires interactive token acquisition to run on the process main thread when the host is not running an AppKit message loop. A console application must therefore drive its work through MacMainThreadScheduler so that SqlConnection.Open resolves on the main thread. Applications that do not do so fail with MsalClientException ("Interactive requests with mac broker enabled must be executed on the main thread on macOS") when interactive sign-in is needed. This does not affect SqlAuthenticationMethod.ActiveDirectoryIntegrated or any flow satisfied from the token cache.
